seoTitle: Free A/B Test Significance Calculator with Sample Size
metaDescription: Test whether variant B beats A with a two-proportion z-test, get the p-value and confidence interval, and estimate the sample size you need. Free.
intro: Enter visitors and conversions for two variants and see the conversion rates, z-score, p-value, whether the difference is significant, and the sample size needed to detect a given lift.
why:
Variant B converts at 5 percent, A at 4 percent, so B wins? Not necessarily. With few visitors a gap like that is often noise, and stopping a test the moment it looks good is a common way to ship changes that do nothing.

This calculator runs a pooled two-proportion z-test and reports the p-value, a confidence interval for the difference, and a clear yes or no at 90, 95 or 99 percent confidence. It also estimates the number of visitors per variant you need to detect a relative lift of your choice, so you can plan the test before you start. It is a standard fixed-sample test, run in your browser.
howTo: Enter visitors and conversions for variant A and variant B.
Choose the confidence level: 90, 95 or 99 percent.
Set the relative lift you want to detect and the power for the sample size estimate.
Read the p-value, the significance verdict, the confidence interval and the required sample size.

faq.a: It is the probability of seeing a difference at least this large if the variants really performed the same. A p-value below 0.05 is significant at 95 percent confidence. It does not give the probability that B is better.

faq.q: Why shouldn't I stop the test as soon as it is significant?
faq.a: Checking repeatedly and stopping at the first significant result inflates false positives. This is a fixed-sample test. Decide the sample size in advance, then evaluate once it is reached.

faq.q: How is the sample size estimated?
faq.a: From the baseline rate of A, the relative lift you want to detect, your confidence and the power, using the standard two-proportion formula. It gives visitors per variant and in total.

faq.q: Does it handle more than two variants?
faq.a: No, only two. For several variants you need to correct for multiple comparisons, which this tool does not do.
